xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2597: Adopt `codex app-server` (JSON-RPC over stdio) as the Codex transport — retire TUI keystroke injection

plan.title: Adopt `codex app-server` (JSON-RPC over stdio) as the Codex transport — retire TUI keystroke injection
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Codex sessions run the interactive TUI in a tmux pane wrapped by the PTY supervisor; every Overdeck->Codex interaction is keystroke emulation plus screen scraping. The conv-795 incident (2026-07-12) showed the failure class: a large composer paste hit a paste-placeholder confirmation regex that only knows Claude Code's format, triggering backspace-purge, full rewrite x2, a throw, and a tmux paste-buffer fallback that stacked a third copy — ending in a ~90% kernel-CPU zero-throughput spin recoverable only by SIGKILL (which kills the session, since the supervisor owns the PTY). Delivery, approvals, readiness, and idle detection are all render-speed-coupled and per-harness-format-fragile.
narratives.Proposal: Adopt `codex app-server` (JSON-RPC over newline-delimited JSON on stdio) as the Codex transport, following the verified t3code reference implementation. A new Overdeck binary, dist/codex-app-server-host.js, runs inside the agent's tmux pane, owns the `codex app-server` child, exposes a token-authenticated per-agent unix socket (message/interrupt/approval/user-input/status ops), renders a readable event feed to the pane, and reads pane stdin as turn input. A message of any size is one turn/start request; approvals, readiness, completion, and interruption are structured protocol events. tmux remains the process/liveness plane, so deacon patrols, pause/kill, and the dashboard terminal work unchanged. Default transport is app-server with a `codex.transport: tui` escape hatch for one release. Conversations and work agents move together.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT delete or modify the existing Codex TUI path (codexMode 'tui'/'work-tui' branches, waitForCodexTuiReady, parseCodexApprovalPrompt, codex supervisor wiring) beyond adding the new dispatch — TUI-path retirement plus its no-loss audit test is the follow-up issue filed at finalize (PRD WI-9, operator-confirmed split)
- No generic large-paste guard for the PTY-injection path (protects Claude Code too) — separate issue per the PRD
- No web rendered-transcript UI replacing the terminal panel — the pane feed keeps the existing terminal surface
- No `codex app-server daemon`/`proxy` shared-daemon modes — one child per agent
- No changes to Pi/ohmypi or Claude Code transports
- No dashboard frontend changes for pane visibility — the host's stdout IS the tmux pane

autoDecisions.summary: PRD checkpoint C2 (protocol-name reconciliation) runs as the first bead: commit the generated JSON schema as a fixture plus a protocol reference doc before any manager code.
autoDecisions.rationale: Cross-cutting protocol assumptions must be pinned before seven beads encode them; codex app-server is [experimental] and 0.144.x is the verified baseline.

autoDecisions.summary: The manager splits into core (spawn/handshake/RPC plumbing) and threads (thread/turn/approval methods) beads; the host splits into core (socket/lifecycle/event log), ops, and pane beads.
autoDecisions.rationale: Independent reviewability per the decomposition rules; safe because nothing spawns the host until the launcher bead flips the default, so partial merges leave the tree working.

autoDecisions.summary: Checkpoint C3 (per-turn model switching) is an acceptance criterion on the host-ops bead with the PRD's restart-with-thread/resume fallback as the stated decision rule.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD names the fallback explicitly; encoding it as a decision rule avoids a judgment call downstream.

autoDecisions.summary: Checkpoint C1 (rollout JSONL under app-server) is a dedicated transcript/cost-continuity bead with the PRD's events-JSONL adapter fallback.
autoDecisions.rationale: FR-9 is user-observable behavior (transcripts, cost) and deserves its own verifiable slice with the fallback decision pre-made.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/codex/app-server-manager.ts, a trimmed port of t3code's codexAppServerManager (reference: /home/eltmon/Projects/t3code/apps/server/src/codexAppServerManager.ts; all citations in PRD WI-2). This bead delivers: (1) child spawn — spawn(codexBinary, ['app-server'], {cwd, env: {...process.env, CODEX_HOME}, stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']}) with readline on stdout (t3code :467-476); (2) pre-spawn version gate — run `codexBinary --version` (4s timeout), semver-compare against 0.144.0, refuse with an actionable upgrade message below the floor (NFR-5); (3) handshake — `initialize` request with {clientInfo:{name:'overdeck',...}, capabilities:{experimentalApi:true}} then `initialized` notification (t3code :500-502); (4) request envelope — integer id counter, pending map keyed by String(id), default 20s timeout, reject on response.error.message (t3code :1191-1247); (5) message classification — server-request (method+id) vs notification (no id) vs response (t3code :1352-1382); invalid JSON lines warn and never crash (t3code :996-1035); (6) stderr handling — strip ANSI, drop non-ERROR lines and the benign 'state db missing rollout path for thread' / 'find_thread_path_by_id_str_in_subdir' messages (t3code :144-149, 397-417). Method/param names come from the spike's protocol doc, not from memory. Build a scripted fake child (a node script replaying canned NDJSON) at src/lib/codex/__tests__/fake-app-server.ts for this and later beads. Repo rules: all timeout tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync; no execSync in server-reachable code.

app-server manager: thread/turn methods, notifications state, approvals, resume fallback

expected_outputs: manager suite passes including 1MB turn/start, approval round-trip, resume fallback, interrupt
typecheck completes without errors

narrative.Action: Extend the manager with the protocol methods and state tracking (t3code :526-736, :817-890, :1072-1189): thread/start with params {model, cwd, approvalPolicy, sandbox, experimentalRawEvents:false}; thread/resume {..., threadId}; turn/start {threadId, input:[{type:'text', text, text_elements:[]}], model?, effort?}; turn/interrupt {threadId, turnId}; thread/read; account/read. Notification state: thread/started captures threadId; turn/started sets running + activeTurnId; turn/completed returns to idle (or error); error notifications use willRetry to distinguish retry from failure. Approvals: store the jsonRpcId of each incoming server request; answer {id, result:{decision}} for approvals and {id, result:{answers}} for user-input. Resume fallback predicate: error message contains 'thread/resume' AND one of 'not found'/'missing thread'/'no such thread'/'unknown thread'/'does not exist' -> thread/start fresh, logging the fallback (t3code :419-426, 562-593). approvalPolicy/sandbox mapping REUSES Overdeck's existing table (src/lib/agents/runtime-command.ts:190-198): full-access -> {approvalPolicy:'never', sandbox:'danger-full-access'}, read-only -> {approvalPolicy:'never', sandbox:'read-only'} pattern, default -> {approvalPolicy:'on-request', sandbox:'workspace-write'}. Model comes from the caller on every thread/turn call — no hardcoded model ID anywhere (NFR-4).

The host composes the manager and: (1) binds ${OVERDECK_HOME}/sockets/appserver-<agentId>.sock at mode 0600 with a token file ${OVERDECK_HOME}/agents/<id>/appserver-token, cloning the pty-token scheme (src/lib/pty-token.ts; socket-bind pattern pty-supervisor.ts:381-398); ops are HTTP-on-unix POSTs with JSON bodies; (2) implements {op:'status'} -> {state: starting|ready|running|awaiting-approval|error|closed, threadId, activeTurnId, pendingRequests:[...]}; (3) appends every protocol event as one JSONL line to ${OVERDECK_HOME}/agents/<id>/appserver-events.jsonl; (4) lifecycle — child exit: render the reason to stdout, close the socket, exit with the child's code (launcher/tmux semantics identical to the PTY supervisor: pane shows the session ended); SIGTERM: turn/interrupt if a turn is running (FR-6), then child SIGTERM, 5s grace, exit — mirror pty-supervisor.ts:455-474. No execSync, no sync tmux primitives anywhere in the host (NFR-1). Message/interrupt/approval ops and the pane feed arrive in the next two beads.

Host ops: message/interrupt/approval/user-input, threadId persistence, per-turn model (checkpoint C3)

narrative.Action: Add the remaining socket ops: {op:'message', content, model?, effort?} -> turn/start; {op:'interrupt'} -> turn/interrupt on the active turn; {op:'approval', requestId, decision} and {op:'user-input', requestId, answers} -> the manager's server-request replies. Model resolution: the op's model wins; else the thread's established default; if neither resolves, return an error and start NO turn — never a hardcoded model (NFR-4). Persist threadId via the existing writeThreadId (src/lib/runtimes/codex.ts:67-91) as soon as thread/started arrives — this replaces the 120s rollout poll in spawn.ts:808-821 for app-server sessions (the poll remains only under transport: tui). Checkpoint C3 decision rule: verify live on codex 0.144.x whether a mid-thread turn/start {model} change takes effect; if yes, pass it through; if not, the host restarts the child and re-attaches with thread/resume under the new model (cursor preserved — t3code reactor pattern). Record which branch was taken in docs/CODEX-APP-SERVER-PROTOCOL.md.

Host pane feed and stdin line input

expected_outputs: pane feed rendering and stdin-to-turn tests pass

narrative.Action: Render a compact, single-writer, plain-text event feed to the host's stdout — which IS the tmux pane: user turns, streamed assistant text, item started/completed lines, approval prompts in the form '[approval #N] command: <cmd> — reply via dashboard or type y/n', and errors. No cursor addressing — the pane is a log, not a UI. Read the host's own stdin with readline, line by line: while an approval is pending, 'y'/'n'/a digit answers it as a decision; any other line becomes a turn/start. This is what makes operator typing in the pane AND the tmux-paste delivery fallback work (FR-3 second leg, FR-7).
